name: Global ID Ordinal Vector Arc Reuse

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Global ID Ordinal Vector Arc Reuse Hypothesis

Because 100% of the 485 warmed global IDs appeared at the same ordinal at both DPRs, a direct previous-frame vector candidate with authoritative full-path equality will eliminate most repeated `Arc<[ElementId]>` allocations without the rejected hash map's lookup and hashing-table overhead.

**Attempt Count:** 1.

### Scope Lock

Add one `Vec<GlobalElementId>` to `WindowFrame`, one collision-safe constructor that may clone the same-ordinal previous ID after full-path equality, one private Window creation path used by all three production constructors, and focused reuse/mismatch assertions. Do not change public APIs, element identity semantics, diagnostics schema, dependencies, unrelated frame storage, or benchmark fixtures.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Run nested formatting, diagnostics-disabled/enabled Clippy with warnings denied, focused and full gpux tests, WGPU tests, then exclusive headed Test Suite WASM/WebGPU proof at both DPRs with CPU profiles. Require exact offsets/counters and zero errors. Compare median acknowledged steps/second, paced p95 catch-up latency, and `Arc<[ElementId]>::from_iter` self time against accepted experiment 102; reject on material throughput or p95 regression even if allocation time falls.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

Retain collision-safe identity behavior, reduce repeated global-ID Arc construction by roughly 80% or more, and avoid the prior hash-map candidate's throughput regression through O(1) ordinal lookup with no auxiliary hashing table.

reportMarkdown:
# Global ID Ordinal Vector Arc Reuse

The single implementation attempt added the scoped ordinal vector, collision-safe full-path reuse constructor, Window creation path, and focused assertions, but failed the first focused compile gate. `element.rs` could not call the Window helper because it was private to the `window` module (`E0624` at both production call sites).

AgentX atomic discipline forbids fixing forward inside the same experiment. Both touched product files were restored byte-for-byte to checkpoint `4e2ce6e59fd107ed974aa17dedbc29daf7a9d8d7`; no runtime or performance measurement was run.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Reject this implementation attempt because it did not compile. Start a new atomic experiment only if the same mechanism is declared with the minimum crate-visible Window helper from the outset; do not attribute any performance result to this failed attempt.
